# superset_user (Resource)

Manages a user in Superset. Requires the Flask-AppBuilder security API, which Superset enables with `FAB_ADD_SECURITY_API = True` in `superset_config.py`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "superset_user" "example_user" {
  username   = "example.user"
  first_name = "Example"
  last_name  = "Sample"
  email      = "example.sample@example.com"
  password   = "ExampleSamplePass123!"
  active     = true
  roles      = [3, 4]
}

# On Superset 6 a user can be made a member of groups from the user side; manage a
# membership either here or in the `users` of the group, not in both.
resource "superset_group" "analysts" {
  name  = "analysts"
  roles = [4]
}

resource "superset_user" "analyst" {
  username   = "analyst.user"
  first_name = "Analyst"
  last_name  = "Sample"
  email      = "analyst.sample@example.com"
  password   = "AnalystSamplePass123!"
  roles      = [4]
  groups     = [superset_group.analysts.id]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `email` (String) Email address of the user.
- `roles` (List of Number) List of role IDs assigned to the user.
- `username` (String) Username of the user.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the user is active. Defaults to true.
- `first_name` (String) First name of the user.
- `groups` (Set of Number) Identifiers of the groups the user is a member of, on Superset 6, for example from `superset_group`. When unset, the memberships are left as they are, as made by the `users` of the groups; when set, the user is a member of exactly these groups, and `[]` removes it from every group. Manage a membership from one side only, here or in `superset_group`. Null on older versions of Superset, which have no groups and reject the attribute.
- `last_name` (String) Last name of the user.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password of the user. Required for creation, optional for updates.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) Numeric identifier of the user.
- `last_updated` (String) Timestamp of the last update.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# User can be imported by specifying the numeric identifier of the User id
terraform import superset_user.example_user 213
```
